South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 04/11/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for COPD management, persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and reassessment of mental health treatment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately two weeks after his last visit. He reports that he has experienced a slight deterioration in his respiratory status over the past week, noting increased shortness of breath and a return of nocturnal wheezing episodes. He states that he has been compliant with his inhaler regimen, using the fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler twice daily, but he has resumed using his albuterol inhaler more frequently, now averaging eight times daily due to worsening symptoms.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant concern. Mr. Fairfax describes the swelling as worsening, now rated at 3+ pitting, particularly in the ankles, and he has noted an increase in discomfort associated with the edema. He has continued dietary sodium restrictions and elevating his legs but feels that the furosemide at 100 mg daily is insufficient.
Additionally, Mr. Fairfax reports that his fatigue has intensified, significantly impacting his daily functioning. He has been adhering to his sertraline regimen but expresses frustration with his mental health status, indicating that his anxiety persists and he has experienced increased mood instability. He expresses a desire for a more effective treatment strategy for his anxiety and depression.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + increased fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + worsening dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + increased joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 84, BP 132/78, RR 24, O2 sat 82% on room air
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, pronounced wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.8, Hgb 10.2, Hct 30.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 128, K 4.2, Cl 98, CO2 25, BUN 32, Cr 1.9, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 700 (increased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax presents with a deterioration in respiratory symptoms, evidenced by increased use of albuterol and worsening nocturnal wheezing. A referral to a pulmonologist is urgently recommended for potential adjustment of inhaled corticosteroids and consideration of a long-acting beta-agonist. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The worsening edema is concerning. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. Given the increase in creatinine levels, a nephrology consult is warranted to assess renal function and consider adjusting diuretic therapy. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. A referral to a psychiatrist for medication review and potential adjustment is advised. Consideration for an augmentation strategy with an alternative antidepressant or anxiolytic may be warranted. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
